transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what’s been bothering you or what brings you in today?

Well, I came in today because I keep getting these... just awful, unwanted thoughts. I constantly feel like I’ve missed something critical. It could be a wrong number in a data release at work, or an unlocked back door at home, or even just a bill paid from the wrong account. 

And the thing is, even when I know I checked it—I know for a fact I looked—my mind just won't let go of the possibility that I’ve caused some sort of disaster. It's really starting to take over my life.
Do you find yourself doing anything repeatedly—like checking, counting, or going over things in your mind—to try to prevent or neutralize these worries?

Yes, I do exactly that. To try and calm myself down, I... I end up reopening spreadsheets I've already closed. I'll reread emails line by line. Or I'll be checking the locks and looking at payment confirmations over and over. 

I actually have to do it all in a specific set order until it finally feels, you know, 'safe' to me. It takes up so much time. Some nights I’m still sitting at my desk hours later, and I have absolutely nothing actually finished because I've just been checking the same things again and again.
Do these unwanted thoughts cause you a lot of anxiety or distress, and do you feel you have to perform these checking behaviors to reduce that anxiety or prevent something bad from happening?

Yes, it causes a tremendous amount of anxiety. It's... it's like this heavy, tight feeling in my chest that just won't go away until I check. I feel like if I don't do my routine—if I don't go through the spreadsheets or check the locks in that exact order—something terrible is going to happen, and it will be entirely my fault. 

The checking is the only thing that gives me any relief, but the relief only lasts for a little while before the dread comes right back. So, yes, I feel like I absolutely have to do it just to make the anxiety stop, even for a minute.
